body: Cases and declines: Super Micro (-86%, 2024), Enphase (~-90%, 2022-25), Celsius (-73%, 2024), Tesla (-73%, 2021-23), Shopify (-87%, 2021-22), Palantir (-87% 2021-22; -36% from Nov 2025 peak while growing 85%), Novo (-73%, 2024-26), Constellation (-51%, 2025-26). Recurring tells visible before or at the top: (1) valuation extremes — P/S >30-100x (Palantir 137x; only 7 other software firms ever exceeded 100x sales and all fell >=70%), P/E ~100x (Celsius, Enphase); (2) gross-margin compression while revenue soars (SMCI 17% -> 11% -> 6%); (3) sell-in outrunning sell-through / distributor inventory build (Celsius-Pepsi, Enphase Europe); (4) demand dependent on a subsidy or rule (Enphase: NEM 3.0, 25D credit); (5) governance history (SMCI's 2018 delisting, prior SEC case; auditor resignation as the final alarm); (6) capex-heavy diversification by an asset-light company (Shopify logistics); (7) peak scarcity in a new category (Novo). Note: in most cases the business stayed real — the loss came from price paid and from one fragile assumption. Process rule: when two or more tells co-occur, cut size or require a much lower entry; never average down after an auditor resigns.
title: Peak-hype reversals: the tells that preceded -70% to -90% falls
